correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the geometric proof for the six-normal regular-dodecagonal norm. The Euclidean comparison yields \(A^2+B^2\ge2+\sqrt3\). For \(B\le1/2\), nonincident edges are excluded because all edge separations at least \(2(2-\sqrt3)>1/2\); independent exact symbolic supporting-functional checks of all five cyclic separation cases corroborate this. On same/adjacent edges signed facets force \(A+(2-\sqrt3)B\ge2\). For \(1<p\le2\), constrained minimization gives \(q=(2-\sqrt3)^{1/(p-1)}\) and the stated first formula, with its minimizer within \(B\le1/2\); concavity of the squared-distance power handles \(B\ge1/2\). For \(p\ge2\), quadratic lower bound and power means give the balanced formula, attained by coordinate unit vectors. Independently recalculated the explicit adjacent-edge extremizers for \(p=1.05,1.4,1.95,2\) and balanced ones for \(p=2.5,3,7\); the numerical checks corroborate but do not establish the all-real exponent theorem. The \(p=1\) triangle-equality case and matching \(p=2\) junction were checked.
